reason: The arterial wall has an unlined inside, so adding the lining cells should help build the outward route from the heart.
expectation: I expect a lined artery with a strong, elastic wall; I don't yet know whether it needs anything else.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and nearby cells clearly fit the exchange goal, but I'll start with the outward route.
The vein also needs a lining, but I'm starting with the artery.

effect: The lined arterial vessels complete the outward-route goal; next I can build the exchange route.
reaction: The arrows away from the heart make the artery's role clear.
reason: Capillaries next to body cells should create the place where blood exchanges materials with them.
expectation: I expect the tiny vessels to sit close to the cells, allowing oxygen and nutrients to move toward them and carbon dioxide away.

alternatives.reason: The venous wall also needs a lining, but I want to build the exchange route before the return route.

effect: The capillary bed shows materials crossing thin walls while blood cells stay inside. I can now build the return route.
reaction: Seeing the different directions of exchange made the capillaries' job clearer.
reason: The venous wall has an unlined inner surface, so lining it should help make the return route.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, probably still needing the one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the artery to the capillary bed makes sense, but I want to prepare the return route first.

effect: The lined veins point toward the heart, but still need valves for the return-route goal.
reaction: The arrows make the return direction clear.
reason: Adding the valve flaps should complete the one-way return route.
expectation: I expect veins with flaps that allow blood to flow toward the heart and help prevent backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Connecting arteries to capillaries also makes sense, but I want to finish the veins first.

effect: The valves complete the return route, and the new goal is to join all three routes.
reaction: The muscle squeezing the vein was a useful detail I hadn't expected.
reason: I'll connect the arteries to the capillaries first, following blood outward from the heart.
expectation: I expect a connected route from the arteries into the capillary bed, still needing the veins.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the capillaries to the veins also fits, but I prefer to follow the route outward first.

effect: The artery and capillaries are connected, leaving open ends for the return route.
reaction: The branching picture makes the route into the capillaries clear.
reason: I'll connect the venous return to the open collecting ends; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a connected route from arteries through capillaries and back through veins.

effect: The final connection completed the route from arteries through capillaries and back through veins.
reaction: Seeing the whole route together made the separate parts feel connected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the capillary bed was most worthwhile: it showed which materials cross the thin walls and that blood cells stay inside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding lining cells to the artery and vein felt a little repetitive, though their different flow directions were clear.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected a nearby contracting muscle to help move blood through a vein while the valves prevent backward flow.

arbitrary.text: None felt particularly arbitrary. The named parts and pictures made their purposes clear, although the compatible-pair menu supplied the options.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter: putting the routes together helped me see how their different jobs connect.
